Guides

Build your website yourself or have it done?

Both options are good, but not for the same people. The real question is not “can I do it?”, it is “do I want to spend my evenings on it?”.

Building your website yourself

Online tools now let you put together a website without writing a line of code. You choose a template, replace the text and photos, and publish.

The advantages:

  • You stay in control of everything, at any time.
  • You learn something useful.
  • The starting cost is low.

The limits:

  • Time. Expect several evenings for a first result, then more time for every change.
  • The blank page. The tool provides the form, not the content. Writing clear text is the hardest part, and nobody does it for you.
  • SEO. A published site is not a site that gets found. The settings that help Google take a bit of know-how.
  • The subscription. These tools are paid every month, and the price often goes up with the features you need.

Having it done

You hand the work to someone who does it for a living: an agency, a freelancer, or a service like mine.

The advantages:

  • You save time, which you spend on your real job.
  • The site is designed to be read, understood and found.
  • Someone answers when something goes wrong.

The limits:

  • The starting price is higher.
  • You depend on the provider's availability for changes.
  • Not all providers are equal: compare what is really included.

Who “do it yourself” is right for

Honestly, do it yourself if you enjoy tinkering, if you have time on your hands, and if your site is not urgent. Some people really enjoy it, and their site looks like them.

Who is better off handing it over

Hand it over if your time is limited, if screens tire you, or if you already have a site you started months ago and never finished. That is the most common case I see.

A third way

My service was born from this. You do not build anything yourself, but you stay in control of what matters:

  • The price is fixed and known in advance, from €250.
  • You request your changes in one sentence from your client area.
  • Lia makes them in 5 minutes and shows you a preview, or I do them by hand within 72 hours. You choose each time.
  • The plan has no commitment.

To see what it looks like before you decide, try the client area demo. And for an overview of the options, the comparison puts them side by side.

Your questions

I started a website myself without finishing it, can you take it over?

I start again from a new site, but nothing is lost: your text, your photos and your ideas serve as a base. Send me the address of what you started, it is an excellent starting point.

If I have my website made, can I still change it?

Yes, without learning anything: you describe the change in your client area. Depending on your plan, Lia makes two to ten changes a month, and Alex one or two.

How long does it take to build a website on your own?

It really depends on the person. The building itself is fairly quick. What takes time is the text, choosing photos and all the small settings you do not think of at the start.
